title: inFAMOUS: Festival of Blood
subtitle: Zeke tells a story with a darker bite

body: inFAMOUS: Festival of Blood is Sucker Punch's standalone PlayStation 3 action game, first released in North America on 25 October 2011. Zeke recounts an exaggerated tale in which Cole MacGrath becomes a vampire, turning the familiar city and powers of inFAMOUS 2 towards a supernatural Halloween adventure. A copy of the larger game is not required. The framing allows the story to step away from the main continuity, using a recognisable hero as the subject of a deliberately unreliable performance. The city becomes a place to explore through abilities that belong to Zeke's unlikely account.

Vampiric powers change the way Cole crosses the city and deals with its inhabitants. Drinking blood restores health, removing the moral structure that shaped choices in the main games. The player is therefore encouraged to inhabit a more monstrous version of the character rather than carefully preserve a familiar heroic alignment. The shorter adventure concentrates on that variation, giving a known environment another atmosphere and another set of practical possibilities. Moving across rooftops and seeking the next objective becomes part of a supernatural story whose narrator has already given himself permission to embellish.

The release also supported PlayStation Move and extended the user-created mission tools with a comic-scene feature. Its music combines contributions from Galactic, Jim Dooley, Brain and JD Mayer. Festival of Blood later joined the first two inFAMOUS games in the PlayStation 3 collection. As a standalone side story, it demonstrates what a familiar game world can support when the normal narrative rules are relaxed. The player recognises Cole and the city, but the telling changes what both can become, making the expansion a purposeful variation rather than another repetition of the main campaign.
